Hi Sara — thanks for the clear note and the CSV. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Laura (finance) so we can scope a clean path. High level: we can do both a conversion and a split, but there are a few trade-offs depending on whether you want the credits to remain promotional (non-invoiceable) or convert to an invoice-backed prepaid balance applied to Dedicated commitments.

Options we typically offer:
- Convert credits to an invoiceable prepay and apply that balance to a Dedicated commit (requires a short addendum to the SOW; benefits: predictable accounting and single invoice).
- Keep credits promotional and assign across sub-accounts (easy operationally but not invoiced; not usable toward Dedicated commit directly).
- Hybrid: convert a portion to invoiced prepay (e.g., 50%) and leave the rest promotional for burst or dev activity.

Questions for you (and CFO):
- Do you need the credits to appear as a prepaid asset on your balance sheet?
- Will the three product teams be billed internally, or is OrbitWorks looking for Redwood to emit separate invoices to each internal cost center?

Ben — quick ask: if we convert 200k promo credits, do you have a standard conversion rate and discount stacking policy to propose? Laura — can you confirm the ops we need on our side for splitting invoices across internal IDs?

I attached a draft SOW template and a stub pricing matrix (see attachments) — I can send a DocuSign link once we agree the path.

Thanks — Kimberly

Kimberly — quick price note from pricing ops.

Conversion mechanics: we treat promo credits as redeemable for hosted usage at a conversion factor tied to the promo program. For a Dedicated conversion, we typically map credits to a dollar-equivalent prepay and then apply it against their Reserved commit. For sizing, if OrbitWorks has 200k credits and program documentation says 1 credit ~= $0.02 of hosted value, that's $4,000 gross.

Discount stacking:
- If they convert to a Dedicated commit, we can propose: convert $4,000 -> apply as prepay toward first-month committed spend.
- For a new Dedicated 3-month pilot, we can offer a one-time 10% conversion top-up (i.e., give them +10% value on the converted dollars) as a limited accelerator exception if they commit to a minimum vGPU-hours or $$ MRR equivalent.
- Separate invoices per internal cost center are supported but add ops overhead: finance will need separate line items and cost-center IDs; there is a $75 per-invoice processing surcharge (one-time) unless they accept a single invoice and handle internal chargebacks.

If OrbitWorks prefers splitting credits across three sub-accounts, we can apportion at conversion time (e.g., 30/40/30) and produce either: (A) three invoices each with its pro-rated prepaid balance, or (B) one invoice with three line items and the cost-center IDs listed (preferred for lower ops overhead).

I'll prepare a suggested pricing matrix with the conversion math and the conditional 10% top-up language.
